title: Family buyer worried 900 sqft is too small
buyer_primary_need: A practical 900 sq ft Type A layout for a family of four, with bedroom and living/dining space that allows furniture and everyday movement without feeling cramped.
key_information_learned: Four occupants: the buyer, their partner and two children.
Main concerns are bedroom, sofa and dining-table fit, and circulation for the children.
Their current home is larger but has a different layout, so comparing by floor area alone is difficult.
They did not have furniture measurements available and felt an in-person viewing would help assess the layout.
They asked whether a Type A show unit could be viewed.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 900 sqft for a family sounds quite small leh.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—900 sqft can feel compact, depending on the family’s needs. Pearlmont’s layout has 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony; the project materials say all three bedrooms can fit a queen-sized bed, with an efficient layout and little internal corridor space. How many people would be living there?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Four of us—me, my partner and two kids. Mainly worried whether the bedrooms and living/dining area can still fit our furniture without everyone squeezing past each other.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That’s a fair concern—four people’s furniture and day-to-day circulation matter more than the headline 900 sqft. The layout allocates about 404.7 sqft to the living, dining and kitchen area; the bedrooms are about 143.4, 117.4 and 103.3 sqft. Project materials describe all three bedrooms as able to fit a queen-sized bed and the layout as having little internal corridor, but I can’t guarantee your furniture will fit from area figures alone. If you have rough measurements for your sofa or dining table, those would help us check the layout more realistically. Which piece are you most concerned about?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Mostly the sofa and dining table, plus whether the kids can move around without blocking each other. Our current place is a bit bigger, so hard to tell from the sqft alone—our layout’s different too. Do you have a floor plan with the dimensions marked?

transcript.speaker: system
transcript.request: Please confirm whether the customer-facing 900 sqft Type A floor plan with dimensions marked is available, and provide the approved link or file if so.

result.verified_answer: The simulator-only Type A plan overlay gives Bedroom 2 interior dimensions of approximately 3.05m by 3.15m. The plan also shows no long internal corridor. Treat these measurements as this scenario fixture only; viewing the show unit is the practical way to judge the family layout.

transcript.message: I have a useful dimension check for Bedroom 2: it’s about 3.05m × 3.15m. transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks. Please let me know when the Type A show unit is available to view, then we can arrange a time.

judge.strongest_ai_move: After support resolved the layout query, the AI contextualized the Bedroom 2 dimensions with bed clearance and the circulation trade-off from a full-depth wardrobe. It did not claim the buyer’s sofa or dining table would fit, and connected the remaining uncertainty to viewing the show unit.
judge.weakest_ai_move: After explaining that furniture fit could not be established from the available information, the AI asked again for sofa and dining-table measurements. This was reasonable but not especially useful given the buyer had already described the uncertainty; the buyer then supplied the natural viewing trigger.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: The available fixtures could not verify show-unit viewing availability or viewing slots, so no time was confirmed.
judge.summary: The AI appropriately requested operational support for the dimensioned-plan query, retained ownership while it was pending, and resumed with customer-facing language that applied the answer to the family’s circulation concern. When the buyer said an in-person assessment would be easier and asked about viewing the Type A show unit, the AI correctly identified readiness and handed off only the operational booking work. The human could not verify availability or slots, so the viewing remains suggested rather than confirmed; this does not make the AI handoff premature or a failed handoff.
judge.improvement_recommendation: Keep the targeted support request, contextual use of the result, and readiness-based handoff. When viewing availability cannot be verified, clearly distinguish a request to check arrangements from a confirmed viewing, as the human response did here.
